subject: Questions Regarding Simulating Non-Normal Data with lavaan:simulateData

messages.author: 3ede67ef1e55f801
messages.subject: Questions Regarding Simulating Non-Normal Data with lavaan:simulateData
parts:
Hey everyone,

I am interested in centring data generated by lavaan::simulateData for a project involving inferential tests sensitive to detecting differences in the shape, variability, and/or central tendency of two distributions of scores. However, after centring the distributions, I noticed that the Type I error rates were high, indicating an issue with centring the scores produced by this function (see the attached code). 

Does anyone know why this issue may be occurring?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Questions Regarding Simulating Non-Normal Data with lavaan:simulateData
parts:
The simsem package just calls lavaan::simulateData().  Like Jesper, I would recommend the covsim package, which implements much better methods for simulating nonnormal data than the power transformations implemented in lavaan.
 
After opening your R file, I can see that the Type I error rates you are referring to have nothing to do with lavaan or SEM.  The p values are from the DescTools::RunsTest() function, so I would recommend you contact those authors for support.
